plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flowers (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. Native to Mexico, it grows outdoors in warm climates and is a holiday staple worldwide as a potted plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in warm regions such as California, Florida, and the Mediterranean, and indoors worldwide
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves called bracts, and the plant needs long nights of about 12+ hours for several weeks to develop its color.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often fragrant flowers that open in late autumn and early winter, brightening gardens when little else is in bloom.
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe's mild regions, and Pacific coastal areas
plants.funFact: Tea oil, used in cooking and hair care in East Asia, is pressed from the seeds of sasanqua and related camellias.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tree that covers itself in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, it blooms with the arrival of early summer, and the fallen flowers carpet streets and sidewalks in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia, New Zealand, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are about 70,000 jacarandas, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low evergreen perennial that produces nodding white cup-shaped flowers with golden stamens, often opening in the cold of early winter and sometimes pushing through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountain woodlands of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true rose; it belongs to the buttercup family and all parts of the plant are toxic.
